metric_rationale: The metric computes the proportion of choices that align with Tallying on the two most diagnostic trials (Trial 1 and Trial 2). In these trials, one option has 3 wins on low-validity features, while the other has 2 wins on high-validity features. Tallying purely counts wins, so it will strongly prefer the option with 3 wins. WADD weights by validity, so it will strongly prefer the option with 2 high-validity wins. Thus, Tallying predicts a value close to 1.0, whereas WADD predicts a value close to 0.0, providing maximal discrimination.

Focuses exclusively on the critical trial (Trial 1) designed to dissociate the two models. Tallying will consistently choose Option A (response 0) because it wins on more features. WADD will more frequently choose Option B (response 1) because the weighted sum of its two highly valid features typically exceeds the weighted sum of A's three less valid features. The mean response on this trial provides a massive and highly reliable contrast between the theories.
